newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO GO ON WITH LOT AIRLINE PARTIAL SELLOFF.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO GO ON WITH LOT AIRLINE PARTIAL SELLOFF.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday decided to proceed with a long-delayed partial privatisation of the national air carrier PLL LOT SA and confirmed that the state would retain a 51-percent stake in the firm after the sell-off.
Finance Minister Marek Belka told a news briefing that the cabinet decided to quickly open a new tender for LOT's [LOT.CN] privatisation adviser.
"The most important decision concerns launching a tender procedure to choose a privatisatiojn adviser," Belka said.
He said that supervision over LOT and its privatisation would be promptly transfered to the treasury ministry from the transport ministry.
The transport ministry had been accused by some analysts of delaying LOT privatisation by dragging its feet on the selection of its adviser.
Last year, the transport minister annulled a tender for LOT's privatisation adviser, saying bidders had demanded excessively high fees.
The government later put off the deadline for the sale to June 30, 1998, from December 31, 1996, saying more studies on the complex process were needed.

Government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska said the cabinet would not ask for changes in a special parliamentary plan for the LOT sell-off, under which the treasury is to retain 51 percent of the firm's shares.
"The government decided not to reduce the treasury's stake (in LOT) below 51 percent," Jakubowska said.
Belka also said that Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, concerned with LOT's poor 1996 results, had ordered an audit of the firm's financial situation.

Last week LOT, impatient with delays in privatisation which has dragged on since 1991, said it would seek its capital to be strengthened by 10 to 15 percent through a new sahre issue in in Poland or abroad or a foreign convertible bond issue.

The company said it had plunged into the red last year but needed to continue expansion to keep apace with rising competition due to liberalisation of international flight regulations. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
